title: Protocol for studying co-infection between SARS-CoV-2 and Staphylococcus aureus in vitro
protocol: Seed 25 cm² and 175 cm² flasks with Vero E6 cells at a density of 1 × 10⁵ cells/mL using 5 mL and 35 mL respectively.
Remove media from the seeded cell flasks on Day 3.
Wash cells twice with 1× PBS.
Dilute virus stock to a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 0.01 in 5 mL of DMEM without supplements.
Calculate the amount of virus needed using the equation: MOI * number of cells / virus stock concentration in PFU/mL.
Add 5 mL of diluted virus to each confluent T175 cm² flask.
Set up a mock infection by adding 2 mL of DMEM without any virus to the 25 cm² flask.
Return all flasks to 37°C, 5% CO₂ incubator for 1 hour.
Gently rock flasks every 10 minutes to re-distribute the inoculum and prevent cells from drying out.
Remove the viral inoculum after 1 hour.
Wash cells once with 1× PBS.
Add 35 mL of DMEM + 2% FBS.
Incubate at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 72 hours or until ∼90% cytopathic effect (CPE) is visible.
Harvest the media from the flasks after incubation.
Centrifuge the harvested media at 500 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant into a new tube.
Aliquot and store the resulting supernatant at −80°C.
Set up 6 well plates of Vero E6 cells two days before performing plaque assays, using a cell density that will ensure 100% confluence after 48 hours.
Seed cells at 5 × 10^4 cells/mL, using 2 mL of media per week for 6 well plates.
Set up 10-fold serial dilutions of virus samples in DMEM without any supplements.
Add 450 μL of DMEM to 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Pipette up and down to mix the contents in each tube.
Discard the tip after mixing.
Take 50 μL from the mixed solution using a sterile tip.
Transfer 50 μL into a new tube containing 450 μL of DMEM.
Continue diluting until reaching a 10−7 dilution.
Remove 6 well plates from the incubator.
Wash the plates once with 1× PBS.
Add 400 μL of virus dilution to each well in the plate.
Return the plate to the incubator at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Gently rock the plates every 10 minutes during incubation.
Prepare an overlay by mixing DMEM with a ratio of 1:1 of 2.4% cellulose in a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Invert vigorously to form a uniform suspension.
Place the tubes in a 37°C water bath to pre-warm.
Remove plates from the incubator and place them in the BSC.
Take overlay tubes from the water bath and place them in the BSC.
Remove inoculum from the 6 well plates.
Pipette up and down to ensure uniform suspension of overlay solution.
Pipette 2 mL per well of the overlay using a serological pipette.
Incubate plates at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 3 days.
Ensure plates are not moved during incubation period.
Remove the plates from the incubator and place them in the BSC.
Add 2 mL per well of 10% Neutral Buffered formalin (NBF) using a serological pipette.
Gently swirl the plates until you can see the cellulose mixture lift up and the NBF is in full contact with the cells.
Incubate at 20°C–23°C for 30 min.
Remove the NBF mixture into a waste basin.
Rinse the cells once-twice with water.
Add 1 mL of Crystal Violet stain per well.
Incubate at 20°C–23°C for 20 min.
Remove the Crystal Violet stain.
Rinse the cells twice with water.
Tap excess water on a paper towel.
Allow plates to dry in the hood for 15–30 min.
Remove plates and count plaques.
Prepare single colony streak plates on Day 1.
Inoculate S. aureus bacteria from frozen glycerol stocks onto TSA plates.
Incubate plates at 37°C for 16–18 hours.
Take a single colony of bacteria and inoculate into 5 mL of TSB in a 30 mL tube.
Incubate at 37°C, 200 rpm for 16-18 hours on Day 2.
Transfer 500 μL of bacteria into a 1.5 mL microfuge tube on Day 3.
Spin the tube at 20,000 × g for 1 minute.
Wash twice with 700 μL of DMEM.
Re-suspend bacteria in 500 μL of DMEM after washing.
Measure optical density (OD) at 600 nm.
Dilute bacteria to a final OD600 of 0.33 in 500 μL of DMEM.
Use a 96 well plate for determining bacterial numbers.
Take 20 μL of the solution to quantify and place it in 180 μL of 1× PBS in well 1.
Pipette up and down to mix.
Discard the tip.
Using a sterile tip, take 20 μL from well 1 and place it into a new well containing 180 μL of 1× PBS.
Continue diluting until a 10−7 dilution is achieved.
Take 10 μL of each dilution and spot them on a 100 mm × 15 mm TSA plate.
Repeat the plating step twice for two replicates at each dilution.
Incubate plates at 37°C for 16–18 hours.
After incubation, select the dilution where 10–40 colonies are present and count the number of colonies.
Take the average count from the two repeats plated.
Calculate CFU/mL using: CFU/mL = (number of colonies) x (dilution factor)/volume plated (mL).
Use 5 μL of a solution with an OD600 of 0.33 in a well of a 12 well tissue culture plate.
This should be the equivalent of 1 × 10^5 CFU/well.
Plate host cells in 12 well plates as per steps 1–3, and streak bacteria strains.
Use 1 mL of media per well for 12 well plates.
Prepare 16–18 h bacterial cultures as per step 7.b.
Infect cells with SARS-CoV-2 and S. aureus.
Prepare your bacterial inoculum as per step 7c.
Work should continue in a CL3 laboratory from the infection step onwards.
Prepare viral inoculum for a confluent 12 well plate with a cell population of 1 × 10^5 cells per well.
Dilute virus stocks for a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 1 in a volume of 100 μL per well of DMEM.
Remove media from 12 well plates.
Wash the plates twice with 1× PBS at approximately 1 mL per well.
Add 100 μL of the virus inoculum prepared to each well.
Ensure a "mock" well receives only 100 μL of DMEM without virus.
Return the plate to 37°C, 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Gently rock plates every 10 minutes to redistribute the inoculum and prevent drying.
Remove plates from the incubator after one hour.
Take off the viral inoculum.
Wash wells twice with 1× PBS.
Add 1 mL of DMEM to each well.
To desired wells, add 5 μL of bacterial inoculum.
Include control samples of mock for virus alone and bacteria alone.
If testing more than one bacterial strain or mutant, ensure you have bacteria only wells for each strain for bacterial counts.
Incubate plates at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
On day 4, harvest infections for bacteria and virus quantification.
Retrieve the plates from the incubator.
Harvest the culture media into 1.5 mL microfuge tubes.
Spin samples at 15,000 × g for 1 minute.
While samples are spinning, add 500 μL of 1× PBS + 0.1% (v/v) Triton X-100 to all wells.
Take the microfuge tubes back into the hood once centrifugation is complete.
Using a 1 mL syringe, gently take the supernatant from the microfuge tube without disturbing the bacterial pellet.
Attach the syringe to a 13 mm, 0.22 μm filter.
Filter the supernatant into a new 1.5 mL microfuge tube.
Harvest the cell lysates in 1× PBS + 0.1% (v/v) Triton X-100 from the wells in step 11.b.
Add the harvested cell lysates to the remaining pellets from step 11.c.
Pipette up and down a few times to re-suspend the pellet.
Perform a serial dilution of this sample.
Plate on TSA plates for CFU enumeration, as described in step 7.c.v.
Incubate plates at 37°C for 18 h.
Infect cells as outlined in steps 8–1o.
Remove culture supernatant after the desired incubation time.
Wash cells three times with 1× PBS.
Add 500 μL of Cell Protect reagent (Qiagen) to each well and incubate at RT for 5 min.
Harvest the wells and centrifuge at 1,200 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Store the pellets at -80°C.
Lyse cell pellets with 500 μL of 1× PBS + 0.1% (v/v) Triton - X100.
Proceed with RNA extraction using the QIAGEN RNeasy kit, as per the manufacturer’s instructions.
Add 600 μL of buffer RLT to the re-suspended cell pellets from the previous step.
Pipette to mix.
Add 1 volume (1.1 mL) of 70% ethanol to the cell lysate and mix well by pipetting.
Transfer 700 μL of the sample from the previous step to an RNeasy spin column and centrifuge for 1 min at 10,000 x g.
Discard the flow through.
Repeat transferring all the lysate through the column until complete.
Add 700 μL of buffer RW1 to the column and centrifuge for 1 min at 10,000 × g.
Discard the flow through.
Add 500 μL of buffer RPE to the column and centrifuge for 2 min at 10,000 × g.
Discard the flow through.
Centrifuge the column for an additional 2 min at 10,000 × g.
Discard the flow through.
Place the RNeasy column into a new 1.5 mL collection tube.
Add 40 μL of water to the membrane and incubate for 1 min at RT.
Centrifuge for 1 min at 10,000 × g.
Repeat step x for a second elution.
Remove samples from CL3 and process the protein as desired.
Follow appropriate decontamination protocols for removing samples from a CL3 laboratory according to local SOPs.
Store RNA samples at −80°C.
Infect cells as outlined in steps 8–10.
Remove culture supernatant after the desired incubation time.
Wash cells three times with 1× PBS.
Add 50 μL of RIPA buffer with protease inhibitor to each well.
Incubate samples on a rocker at 4°C for 30 min.
Centrifuge samples at 12,000 × g for 20 min.
Harvest the resulting supernatant and place it in a new tube.
Remove plates from step 11.e from the incubator after 5 days.
Count colonies and calculate CFU per mL.
Mock infect or infect Vero E6 cells with CoV-2 at MOI of 1 for 1 hour.
Overlay infected Vero E6 cells with 1 mL of serum-free DMEM.
Add 1 × 10^5 CFU of WT S. aureus strain USA300 to the culture media.
Incubate the cultures for 24 hours at appropriate conditions.
Harvest DMEM from the cultures after incubation.
Centrifuge samples for 1 minute at 15,000 × g.
Add 500 μL PBS + 0.1% v/v Triton X-100 to the tissue culture wells.
Remove supernatant and resuspend pellet in 500 μL PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 from the wells.
Serially dilute bacteria and plate on TSA plates.
Incubate plated samples at 37°C for 18 hours.
Enumerate CFU from the plates.
Infect Vero E6 cells with SARS-CoV-2 at an MOI of 1 for 1 hour.
Overlay infected cells with 1 mL of serum-free DMEM.
Add 1 × 10^5 CFU of WT S. aureus strain USA300 to the culture media.
Incubate the co-infected cultures for 24 hours.
Harvest DMEM from the wells after incubation.
Centrifuge samples at 15,000 x g for 1 minute.
Filter the resulting supernatant through a 0.22 μm filter.
Dilute the filtered samples serially.
Quantify viral titer by plaque assay.
Filter the virus-only samples using the same method as co-infected samples.
Ensure that filtering results in a decrease of PFU/mL by approximately 1 log.
